title.narrative: Support Nigeria to advance inclusive quality education and lifelong learning

description.narrative:
Beyond the effect of COVID-19, inclusion in education is further challenged in Nigeria due to emerging insecurities that have threatened the safety of schools and ultimately denying some learners their right to education. As a result of the crises of insecurity, children of school age in some parts of Nigeria, particularly the Northern region have limited and in some cases no access to school. More worrisome, is the plight of learners with special needs, as infrastructure/equipment to aid their learnings are not available. The increasing emergencies that interrupt school systems and ultimately learning requires systemic preparedness that will ensure that learning continues without leaving anyone behind.
It is in this regards that the implementation of the right to education, including creating lifelong learning opportunities will be pursued within the 42 C5 programmes and activities. To achieve this, UNESCO will strengthen partnerships and networks to promote cross-sectoral collaboration that will stimulate technical dialogues, policies and practices that assures the learning needs of marginalized groups.
ICH will be addressed through Education, and States including the FCT, would be engaged to review ESP to ensure inclusive education is mainstreamed and budgeted for. Cross-sectoral collaboration with health, nutrition and social protection will be encouraged.
